An atlas of the Anglo-Indian wars · 1686–1947

A trading company took a subcontinent.
This is where, and how fast.

In 1686 the East India Company held three fortified towns and lost a war to the Mughal emperor. By 1900 it and its successor governed or protected 97 per cent of the land on this map. Drag the timeline along the bottom and watch it happen.

Ruled outright Held by treaty — a prince kept his throne and lost his army Beyond British power

That distinction is the argument of the whole atlas: by 1900 rather more of India was governed through the hatching than through the solid colour.
